story.h2:
This started because three
multi-effects units cost a fortune.
story.p1: My son started guitar lessons. His teacher had one sound, we had another one at home, and what he learned in the lesson didn't happen again afterwards. Fixing that by buying everyone the same unit cost more than the instrument.
story.p2: I've been a developer for 26 years. At the time I was investigating, with method, how far you can go programming with AI — and a study like that is only worth anything if the problem is hard. Live audio is hard: the code runs a few hundred times a second and, when it gets it wrong, the sound fails right there, in front of everyone. There's no hiding it.
story.p3: It worked out better than I expected. OpenRig today is a real-time audio platform written in Rust: every input is an isolated runtime, so two guitars on the same interface really are two independent rigs. Amp, cab and pedal mixing native DSP, neural captures and IRs in the same chain. Presets in plain text you can open and edit.
story.p4: And the original idea grew with it: instead of one tone for me and my son, one computer on stage processing the whole band, each musician working on their own sound. Only one of them needs the gear.
road.lede: All of it is public. Each line is an issue on GitHub you can read, comment on or pick up.
road.done.i1: Chain editor with real knobs, drag to reorder
road.done.i2: Five backends in one rig — native, NAM, LV2, VST3, IR
road.done.i3: Capture packs turn into knobs on their own
road.done.i4: Presets and scenes switching without a gap in the sound
road.done.i6: Looper, DI loop, metronome, tuner, spectrum, Tone Doctor
road.done.i7: MCP server and the Claude skills
road.done.i8: Several interfaces at once, insert loop for hardware
road.next.i4: Global tap tempo and expression pedal
road.next.i5: Trim and reuse a recorded loop
road.next.i6: Footswitch profile editor inside the app
road.later.i5: More native DSP modelled from papers
road.note: Want something moved up the list? Open an issue.
fund.lede: OpenRig has no company behind it and nothing to sell you. It stays free and open source either way — money decides how fast it moves and how many machines it runs on.
fund.c1.p: Audio interfaces, footswitches and a Windows and a Linux machine to build and test on. Right now it's whatever is already in the room.
fund.c2.p: Capture packs, licences and studio time to model amps properly instead of guessing.
fund.c3.p: Every hour funded is an hour on the list above.
fund.note: No tiers, no paywalled features, no "pro" version. Ever.
dl.lede: OpenRig is free and open source. Download it, open it and start playing — nothing to sign up for, nothing to unlock later.
